text: Every galaxy in this box is sitting perfectly still. Nothing here is flying anywhere. Watch what happens to them anyway.
You are the bright blue one in the middle. Let time run forward.

Every single galaxy is moving away from you, and the further one is, the faster it goes. That is not an explosion pushing things outward. The galaxies are not moving. The distance between them is growing.

Look at the chart. Distance along the bottom, speed up the side, and the points fall on a straight line. Hubble measured that line in nineteen twenty nine, and its slope is the expansion rate of the universe.
Here is the part that trips almost everyone up. If everything is running away from us, surely we are at the centre of it. So let me move you.
You are now a galaxy at the far corner of the box, thousands of millions of light years from where you were. And the chart is identical. Same straight line, same slope.
Try another one at random. And another. It never changes. Every galaxy sees itself at the centre, which is the same as saying there is no centre at all.
Now wind the clock backwards instead. The scale factor is the size of the universe compared to today, and I am taking it down to a fifth.

Everything is packed five times closer together. Light leaving a galaxy at this moment arrives at us stretched out by a factor of five. That stretching is redshift, and it is how we know how far back we are looking.

Back to today. Notice the readout that says some galaxies are receding faster than light. That is allowed. Nothing is travelling through space faster than light. There is simply more space appearing between us than light can cross.

One last thing, and it is an open problem. The expansion rate measured from the early universe is sixty seven point four. Measured from nearby stars and supernovae, it is seventy three. Both teams are careful. Watch the age of the universe when I switch.

The universe just got about a billion years younger, and nobody knows which number is wrong. That disagreement is called the Hubble tension, and it is one of the biggest unsolved problems in cosmology right now. The controls are yours.
